decisions.summary: Bound how long a check-wave row waits for an agent (WAVE_WAIT_S after its dispatch), asked by both readers of the wait (handle::concerns, rounds::pair_wave), with Row keeping t for concerns, so a SubagentStop no row names neither books nor rewrites the 2.6 MB check state.
decisions.why: Performance work on the checks' tooling is what the GM asked to come first (2026-11-20, 'can we in general priotitize performance improvements going forward?'; FR-013), and this one is measured before and after (89.6/94.3 -> 14.1/14.3 ms CPU, writes 22 of 22 -> 0 of 22). It takes cost off every subagent stop and narrows nothing the request or spec asks for.

decisions.summary: WAVE_WAIT_S is 6 hours, a GUESS knob labeled in its doc comment as HOLD_MAX_S is, timed from the dispatch t; a pending row past it stops waiting too; WAVE_PENDING_S unchanged.
decisions.why: Picking the knob's value and what it is timed from is a design choice inside the perf fix. 6 h is many times the longest wave agent measured (585 s over 362 agents), so no wave inside its own run is affected. A pending row is already dead to live after WAVE_PENDING_S (30 min), so a pending row that stops waiting at 6 h changes nothing anyone relies on. Nothing in the request sets this value.

decisions.summary: An agent paired after the wait is treated as one no row names: its reply, round and EDIT blocks are not booked; the row stays returned-with-no-reply as before; said in the doc comment.
decisions.why: This is the cost of the age bound, stated and not hidden. It only reaches a wave unit retried more than 6 h after its wave's dispatch, against a measured longest run of 585 s, and it leaves the row as it stood before the late agent came. That is not a wrong outcome on any path the request or the spec names, so it is not a defect left and not a narrowing of what was asked.

decisions.summary: Choose the age bound over saving only when a booking changed a row, because comparing needs the whole parse (the 55 ms clone and compare T387 removed).
decisions.why: Choosing between two ways to make the same perf improvement is design, not fidelity. Neither option narrows the request.

decisions.summary: The skipped keys are scanned with an exact visitor (Skip, through deserialize_any), and malformed shapes fall back to the whole parse. The cheaper IgnoredAny scan (about 5 to 8 ms a hook more saved) is priced and filed as T506, to land before T302.
decisions.why: This defers a further speedup. It is not a defect: no answer is wrong, nothing crashes, and no valid input is refused. It is filed as T506 with an order before T302 (FR-009) and is scheduled first as perf work under FR-013, so nothing the GM asked for is cut. The block names no wrong outcome under the cheaper scan on a state that can occur. Its only stated reason is acceptance parity on texts no writer produces (1e400, a lone surrogate), and that parity is the brief's wording, not the GM's. Under the no-exactness standard, parity is not a reason to refuse the cheaper scan. T506 must be judged on whether everything works, for example whether a hot hook could pass on a state the gate refuses in practice. Differing acceptance of texts no writer emits is not a ground to keep the slower scan. The exact scan stands for now only because the deferral loses nothing.

decisions.why: These tests check that a pure refactor of the reader changes no outcome. blocks: ### T505 (451 T490: every SubagentStop booked and rewrote the whole 2.6 MB check state, 92 to 95 ms of CPU a stop and 22 of 22 writing, because 14 check-wave rows `returned` with no reply, 861 to 863 hours old, still counted as waiting for an agent, measured 2026-11-27 (`t490-time.py`'s agent-stop arm, 20 runs))

decisions.summary: Bound how long a check-wave row waits for an agent (WAVE_WAIT_S after its dispatch), asked by both readers of the wait (handle::concerns, rounds::pair_wave), with Row keeping t for concerns, so a SubagentStop no row names neither books nor rewrites the 2.6 MB check state.
decisions.why: Performance work on the checks' tooling is what the GM asked to come first (2026-11-20, 'can we in general priotitize performance improvements going forward?'; FR-013), and this one is measured before and after (89.6/94.3 -> 14.1/14.3 ms CPU, writes 22 of 22 -> 0 of 22). It takes cost off every subagent stop and narrows nothing the request or spec asks for.

decisions.summary: WAVE_WAIT_S is 6 hours, a GUESS knob labeled in its doc comment as HOLD_MAX_S is, timed from the dispatch t; a pending row past it stops waiting too; WAVE_PENDING_S unchanged.
decisions.why: Picking the knob's value and what it is timed from is a design choice inside the perf fix. 6 h is many times the longest wave agent measured (585 s over 362 agents), so no wave inside its own run is affected. A pending row is already dead to live after WAVE_PENDING_S (30 min), so a pending row that stops waiting at 6 h changes nothing anyone relies on. Nothing in the request sets this value.

decisions.summary: An agent paired after the wait is treated as one no row names: its reply, round and EDIT blocks are not booked; the row stays returned-with-no-reply as before; said in the doc comment.
decisions.why: This is the cost of the age bound, stated and not hidden. It only reaches a wave unit retried more than 6 h after its wave's dispatch, against a measured longest run of 585 s, and it leaves the row as it stood before the late agent came. That is not a wrong outcome on any path the request or the spec names, so it is not a defect left and not a narrowing of what was asked.

decisions.summary: Choose the age bound over saving only when a booking changed a row, because comparing needs the whole parse (the 55 ms clone and compare T387 removed).
decisions.why: Choosing between two ways to make the same perf improvement is design, not fidelity. Neither option narrows the request.
